The primary data (for establishing safety and efficacy) is based on 26-week data from **GS-US-200-4625** (CAPELLA), described by the Applicant as a “partially randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind multicenter trial.”

population.text: Heavily treatment-experienced (HTE) adults with multidrug-resistant (MDR) HIV-1 infection failing their current regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations.

citations.quote: GS-US-200-4625 (CAPELLA) [NCT04150068]	HTE adult and adolescent subjects with MDR HIV-1 infection

Efficacy of lenacapavir (LEN) in HTE patients with multidrug resistance (MDR) who were failing treatment due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations was established in Study GS-US-200-4625 (Study 4625), a phase 2/3 study conducted in two cohorts.

endpoint.text: Primary: proportion of subjects in Cohort 1 achieving a reduction in HIV-1 RNA of ≥0.5 log10 copies/mL from baseline at the end of the functional monotherapy period (FMP) at Day 14.

citations.quote: Primary: The proportion of subjects in Cohort 1 achieving a reduction in HIV-1 RNA of ≥0.5 log10 copies/mL from baseline at the end of the FMP
Superiority of LEN compared to placebo was demonstrated for the proportion of HIV-1 RNA reduction \ge 0.5 \log_{10} from baseline to the end of the functional monotherapy period (FMP) at Day 14.

result.text: Primary endpoint met: 87.5% of SUNLENCA subjects (N=24) vs 16.7% of placebo (N=12) achieved ≥0.5 log10 decrease in viral load at end of FMP; treatment difference 70.8% (95% CI 34.9% to 90.0%). At Week 52, 83.3% of Cohort 1 achieved HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥3%, all grades) were injection site reactions (65%) and nausea (4%). Injection site reactions were the most frequent AE; nodules and indurations may persist. 96% of adverse reactions were mild or moderate; 1% discontinued SUNLENCA due to an AE (Grade 1 injection site nodule).

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (all Grades) reported in at least 3% of subjects in CAPELLA were nausea and injection site reactions.

Adverse Reactions	SUNLENCA + Background Regimen (N=72)
Injection Site Reactions	65%
Nausea	4%
The majority (96%) of all adverse reactions associated with SUNLENCA were mild or moderate in severity.
The proportion of subjects in CAPELLA who discontinued treatment with SUNLENCA due to adverse events, regardless of severity, was 1% (Grade 1 injection site nodule in 1 subject).
